cards.name: ExtendScript language and runtime
cards.summary: AE scripts are ExtendScript (.jsx): JavaScript at ECMA-262 3rd edition (ES3) plus E4X, File/Folder, ScriptUI, Socket and the $ debug object.
use_for: deciding what JavaScript syntax a generated script may use
cards.how: Write .jsx files; run via File > Scripts > Run Script File, the Scripts / ScriptUI Panels folders, or AfterFX.exe -r. Generated scripts should stick to ES3 (var, function, for loops; no let/const, arrow functions, template strings, Array.map/forEach, JSON). Debug helpers: getEnumAsString(layer.blendingMode) -> 'BlendingMode.SCREEN' (24.0+), isValid(obj), $.writeln() to the debugger console, timeToCurrentFormat(t, fps).
cards.script_api: ExtendScript global scope: app, system, $, File, Folder, alert(); getEnumAsString(enum) (24.0), isValid(obj), generateRandomNumber(), timeToCurrentFormat(time, fps[, isDuration]), currentFormatToTime(str, fps[, isDuration]); app.version (string, e.g. '26.0x67': parseFloat(app.version) gives 26), app.buildNumber
cards.limits: ES3 only: no native JSON object, so pass data in as a JS literal (AdobeBridge prepends `var S = <json>;` built with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True)). Docs say any UTF-8 .jsx is accepted, but AdobeBridge saw non-ASCII garbled on -r runs and keeps every script pure ASCII (field-tested in AdobeBridge). .jsxbin may not work with every integration feature.

cards.name: Run a script from the command line (AfterFX.exe -r / -s)
cards.summary: Send a .jsx file (-r) or a script string (-s) to the already-running After Effects instance from a shell or another program.
use_for: pipeline-driven builds (AdobeBridge runs every AE job this way)
batch jobs without touching the UI
cards.how: afterfx.exe -r C:\full\path\job.jsx  (runs in the existing instance; does not start a second one). app.exitAfterLaunchAndEval (Windows only) quits AE after a -r/-s launch; app.exitCode returns a status to the command line.
cards.script_api: AfterFX.exe -r <file> | -s "<script>"; app.exitAfterLaunchAndEval; app.exitCode
cards.limits: Field-tested limits (field-tested in AdobeBridge): a relative -r path is resolved against AE's own cwd and silently ignored, so pass an absolute path; launch through PowerShell Start-Process with an 8.3 short path (quoting the path made AE ignore the script; launching from a hidden parent made AE run the job and quit). AE can go deaf to every later -r after a MOGRT export, after its open .aep was deleted, or after app.open/close from inside a script: run a cheap canary after each job and force-restart AE when it stops answering. A crash-recovery dialog (after a force-kill) and a disk-cache 'Warning' dialog block all -r jobs until dismissed. Scripts have no stdout: report results through the saved project (AdobeBridge writes 'AB_WARN ... ~' comp names and greps the .aep bytes).

cards.name: aerender command-line renderer
cards.summary: aerender.exe renders comps or the whole render queue of a project from the command line, in a new headless AE instance or (with -reuse) the running one.
use_for: final renders after a scripted build
rendering one comp or one render-queue item to a chosen file
cards.how: "C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe After Effects 2026/Support Files/aerender.exe" -project p.aep -comp "Main" -RStemplate "Best Settings" -OMtemplate "H.264 - Match Render Settings - 40 Mbps" -output out.mp4. Other flags (from aerender -help, v26.0x67): -rqindex, -renderSettings "key: value; ...", -outputSettings, -s/-e/-i frames, -mem_usage, -mfr ON|OFF max_cpu, -v ERRORS|ERRORS_AND_PROGRESS, -close DO_NOT_SAVE_CHANGES|SAVE_CHANGES|DO_NOT_CLOSE, -reuse, -log, -sound ON|OFF, -version, -continueOnMissingFootage, -teamproject.
cards.script_api: aerender.exe (not an ExtendScript object); in-app equivalent app.project.renderQueue.render(); network rendering: app.watchFolder(folder), app.pauseWatchFolder(pause), app.endWatchFolder(), app.isWatchFolder, app.isRenderEngine
cards.limits: Without -comp/-rqindex it renders the whole queue as saved and ignores -RStemplate/-OMtemplate/-output/-s/-e/-i. Template names must exist exactly or it errors. A new instance always closes and quits when done. Without -reuse it starts a second AE (heavy on an 8 GB-VRAM laptop). Watch-folder rendering on another machine needs collected files and the same fonts/plug-ins there; aerender over SSH is simpler for one worker. -close defaults to DO_NOT_SAVE_CHANGES, so -reuse closes the project open in the running AE after the render unless you pass -close DO_NOT_CLOSE (and closing the open project is one of the things that has left AE deaf to -r here). With -reuse AE also writes its preferences on quit.

cards.name: Allow Scripts To Write Files And Access Network (preference)
cards.summary: Security preference that gates File writes, Socket/network access and similar from scripts; off by default.
use_for: deciding how a script reports results
any script that writes logs, JSON or sidecar files
cards.how: Edit > Preferences > Scripting & Expressions > Allow Scripts To Write Files And Access Network (moved there from General in CC 2019; older docs still say General).
cards.script_api: read-only check: app.preferences.getPrefAsLong('Main Pref Section v2', 'Pref_SCRIPTING_FILE_NETWORK_SECURITY') -> 1 on / 0 off (key found in 'Adobe After Effects 26.0 Prefs.txt', the default PREF_Type_MACHINE_SPECIFIC file; value is "0" on this machine). Key name is not in the scripting guide.
cards.limits: It is the user's setting: do not flip it from a pipeline. It is OFF on this machine, so AdobeBridge reports through the saved .aep (warning comps named 'AB_WARN ... ~') instead of writing files (field-tested in AdobeBridge). Saving the project and rendering are not blocked by it. The scripting guide's overview page still says Preferences > General; that text predates the move.

cards.name: BridgeTalk inter-application messaging (AE -> Premiere)
cards.summary: ExtendScript's BridgeTalk sends a script string from one Adobe app to another; AdobeBridge uses it because Premiere has no -r flag.
use_for: driving Premiere Pro from an AE job
cards.how: In AE: if (!BridgeTalk.isRunning('premierepro')) BridgeTalk.launch('premierepro'); var bt = new BridgeTalk(); bt.target = 'premierepro'; bt.body = 'eval(decodeURIComponent("<percent-encoded script>"))'; bt.send();  Optional bt.onResult / bt.onError callbacks.
cards.script_api: BridgeTalk.isRunning(spec), BridgeTalk.launch(spec[, where]), BridgeTalk.getSpecifier(), new BridgeTalk(): .target, .body, .onResult, .onError, .send([timeout])
cards.limits: BridgeTalk re-escapes backslashes and quotes in the body; percent-encode the whole payload and decodeURIComponent it first thing (field-tested in AdobeBridge). If AE has gone deaf to -r the relay never fires: watch for the Premiere job's start marker and restart AE after ~60 s.

cards.name: UXP vs ExtendScript status (2026)
cards.summary: AE has no UXP scripting yet (Adobe plans a public UXP plugin beta by November 2026); ExtendScript stays the AE scripting API. Premiere has UXP since 25.6, and Adobe says ExtendScripts are not affected by the CEP-to-UXP transition.
use_for: choosing the automation technology for AdobeBridge
cards.how: Keep AE automation in ExtendScript (.jsx). CEP panels: AE stops new CEP submissions and disables CEP by default in December 2028; Premiere stops new CEP submissions December 2027, disabled by default December 2028; CEP removed from new versions December 2029.
cards.script_api: AE: ExtendScript only; Premiere: ExtendScript and UXP (premierepro module, async API)
cards.limits: AE UXP is announced, not shipped: as of 2026-10-03 there is no AE UXP beta yet (target: November 2026), so treat any 'AE UXP' API as unavailable. Premiere UXP needs v25.6+ (developer.adobe.com prerequisites). Adobe promises at least two years between the AE UXP beta and CEP removal.

cards.name: ExtendScript Toolkit (ESTK) -> VS Code ExtendScript Debugger
cards.summary: The ExtendScript Toolkit is deprecated and unmaintained (and does not run on 64-bit-only macOS); Adobe's ExtendScript Debugger extension for VS Code is the official replacement.
use_for: inspecting the object model while writing builders
cards.how: Install 'ExtendScript Debugger' (Adobe.extendscript-debug) in VS Code, pick After Effects 2026 as the target, run or debug the .jsx. The extension can also export .jsxbin (UI or command line). 'File > Scripts > Open Script Editor' in the AE guide refers to ESTK.
cards.script_api: none (developer tool)
cards.limits: Do not plan around ESTK. Whether the VS Code extension offers an equivalent of ESTK's Object Model Viewer is unverified. .jsxbin may not work with every AE integration feature (AE guide).

cards.name: Undo groups
cards.summary: Wrap a script's edits into one Edit > Undo entry.
use_for: making a whole scripted build undoable in one step
keeping the user's undo history clean
cards.how: app.beginUndoGroup('AdobeBridge build'); ...edits...; app.endUndoGroup();  Pairs may nest; inner names are ignored.
cards.script_api: app.beginUndoGroup(undoString), app.endUndoGroup()
cards.limits: If the script never calls endUndoGroup, AE closes the group when the script ends; calling endUndoGroup without a beginUndoGroup throws. Some calls are documented as not undoable (Project.replaceFont).

cards.name: Error handling and uncatchable failures
cards.summary: Script errors raise exceptions or modal dialogs; app.beginSuppressDialogs()/endSuppressDialogs() suppress script error dialogs, app.onError names a callback for errors (useful during renders), app.saveProjectOnCrash=false skips the save-on-crash dialog, and app.exitCode reports a status to a -r/-s caller.
use_for: unattended builds that must not stop on a modal dialog
cards.how: app.beginSuppressDialogs(); try { ... } catch (e) { record(e); } app.endSuppressDialogs(false); app.onError = function (s) { ... };
cards.script_api: app.beginSuppressDialogs(), app.endSuppressDialogs(alert), app.onError (callback gets error string and severity), app.saveProjectOnCrash, app.exitCode, isValid(obj)
cards.limits: Field-tested in AdobeBridge: some failures end the script with no catchable error and no dialog: setting a number outside a property's min/max (clamp with hasMin/minValue/hasMax/maxValue first), for-in over undefined, asking a non-group property for a child (CC effects' 'Producer'/'Physics' header rows are PropertyType.PROPERTY), and touching a Project object after a MOGRT export ('Object is invalid'). Leave a breadcrumb after each host call so the last one locates the failure.

cards.name: Menu command fallback (app.executeCommand)
cards.summary: Runs any menu command by numeric ID; the only route to features with no scripting API.
use_for: UI-only commands such as Convert To Bezier Path, Easy Ease, layer styles
anything missing from the object model
cards.how: Find the ID once during development with app.findMenuCommandId('Exact Menu Text'), then hard-code the number: app.executeCommand(4162) // Convert To Bezier Path (docs example). Select the target layers/properties and make sure the right comp viewer is active first.
cards.script_api: app.executeCommand(id), app.findMenuCommandId(commandText)
cards.limits: findMenuCommandId is not reliable across language packs; IDs can change between versions; commands act on the current selection/active panel, so they fail silently when focus is elsewhere. No return value to confirm success: read the result back.

cards.name: Application control: scheduled tasks and restart
cards.summary: Run a JavaScript string after a delay (once or repeatedly) inside AE, and restart AE from a script (app.restart, added 25.4).
use_for: polling a job folder from inside AE
deferring work until AE finishes an operation
cards.how: var id = app.scheduleTask("$.writeln('tick')", 1000, true); ... app.cancelTask(id);  app.restart();
cards.script_api: app.scheduleTask(stringToExecute, delayMs, repeat), app.cancelTask(taskID), app.restart() (25.4)
cards.limits: Scheduled strings run in global scope; a repeating task runs until cancelled or AE quits. app.restart ends the current script (whether it prompts to save is unverified) and cannot help when AE already ignores scripts: AdobeBridge restarts from outside instead (taskkill, relaunch, answer Crash Repair with Continue).

cards.name: Memory, cache and rendering switches
cards.summary: Purge caches, cap memory, switch rendering off (Caps Lock equivalent) or set Multi-Frame Rendering for the next render.
use_for: long batch builds that bloat RAM
speeding up a build by disabling viewer rendering
cards.how: app.purge(PurgeTarget.ALL_MEMORY_CACHES); app.disableRendering = true (set back to false at the end); app.setMultiFrameRenderingConfig(true, 80); app.setMemoryUsageLimits(imageCachePct, maxMemPct).
cards.script_api: app.purge(PurgeTarget.ALL_CACHES|ALL_MEMORY_CACHES|UNDO_CACHES|SNAPSHOT_CACHES|IMAGE_CACHES), app.disableRendering, app.setMultiFrameRenderingConfig(mfr_on, max_cpu_perc), app.setMemoryUsageLimits(), app.memoryInUse
cards.limits: Since 24.3 ALL_CACHES also clears the disk cache (ALL_MEMORY_CACHES = RAM only). The MFR setting resets to the UI value after the script ends.

cards.name: Installed effects list (app.effects)
cards.summary: Read-only array of every effect AE has: displayName, matchName, category, version. The authoritative existence check before adding an effect.
use_for: validating a plan's effect names before a build
mapping display names to match names
cards.how: for (var i = 0; i < app.effects.length; i++) if (app.effects[i].matchName == 'ADBE Gaussian Blur 2') ...  Apply with layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty(matchName).
cards.script_api: app.effects[i].displayName / .matchName / .category / .version
cards.limits: displayName and category are localized; matchName is stable across versions and languages, so plans should store match names. A lookup that cannot fail is not an existence check: test against this list (or canAddProperty) rather than the truthiness of an add.

cards.name: Preferences and Settings objects
cards.summary: Read and write AE preference-file keys (app.preferences) and script settings (app.settings), persisted between sessions.
use_for: reading a preference before a build
cards.how: app.settings.saveSetting('AdobeBridge', 'lastRun', '...'); app.settings.getSetting(...); app.preferences.getPrefAsLong(section, key[, PREFType.PREF_Type_MACHINE_SPECIFIC]).
cards.script_api: app.preferences.getPrefAsBool/Long/Float/String, savePrefAsBool/Long/Float/String, havePref, deletePref, reload, saveToDisk; app.settings.getSetting/saveSetting/haveSetting
cards.limits: Exact section/key names for built-in preferences are undocumented; writing AE's own preferences changes the user's setup (don't). Values are strings in the file.

cards.name: Shell commands from a script (system.callSystem)
cards.summary: Run an OS command line from ExtendScript and get its text output.
use_for: calling ffmpeg or python from inside an AE job
cards.how: var out = system.callSystem('cmd.exe /c "ffprobe -v error ..."');
cards.script_api: system.callSystem(cmdLine); system.osName, system.machineName, system.userName
cards.limits: Blocks AE until the command finishes. Whether the file/network preference gates it is unverified. Prefer doing shell work in the Python runner outside AE.

cards.name: Project create / open / save / close
cards.summary: Create, open, save and close .aep projects from a script.
use_for: saving the built project for Premiere/aerender
cards.how: var proj = app.newProject(); ...; proj.save(new File('C:/out/name_v2.aep'));  app.open(file) opens a project; proj.close(CloseOptions.DO_NOT_SAVE_CHANGES).
cards.script_api: app.newProject(), app.open([file]), app.openFast(file) (undocumented), Project.save([file]), Project.saveWithDialog(), Project.close(closeOptions), Project.dirty (17.5, officially undocumented), Project.file
cards.limits: Field rule (AdobeBridge memory + field-tested in AdobeBridge): never app.open/close a project from inside a pipeline script, and never overwrite or delete the .aep AE has open; both have left AE deaf to later -r jobs. Version output names (_v2, _v3) instead. Check app.project.dirty and refuse to clobber the user's unsaved work. save() without a file on a never-saved project opens a dialog. app.newProject() asks the user to save an edited current project (modal) and returns null if they cancel; app.open() with no file opens a dialog.

cards.name: Project items and stable IDs: comps, folders, lookup
cards.summary: Create comps and folders, find items by index, ID or selection, and find layers by their persistent ID (Layer.id / Project.layerByID, 22.0+).
use_for: mapping plan items to built layers across script runs
cards.how: var comp = app.project.items.addComp('Main', 1920, 1080, 1, 30, 30);  // name, w, h, pixelAspect, durationSec, fps. app.project.items.addFolder('Footage'); item.parentFolder = folder; app.project.item(i) is 1-based. var id = layer.id; ... app.project.layerByID(id).
cards.script_api: Project.items (ItemCollection.addComp(name, width, height, pixelAspect, duration, frameRate), addFolder(name)), Project.item(index), Project.itemByID(id), Project.activeItem, Project.selection, Project.rootFolder, Item.id/.name/.comment/.label/.remove(), Layer.id (22.0), Project.layerByID(id) (22.0)
cards.limits: Indices are 1-based and shift when items or layers are added/removed; keep IDs for stable references. Layer IDs survive save/reload but are reassigned when the project is imported into another project.

cards.name: Import footage and image sequences
cards.summary: Import files (video, audio, stills, PSD/AI as comps, image sequences) into the project.
use_for: bringing clips, music, PNG overlays into a build
importing a PSD as a layered comp
cards.how: var io = new ImportOptions(new File(path)); io.sequence = true; if (io.canImportAs(ImportAsType.COMP)) io.importAs = ImportAsType.COMP; var item = app.project.importFile(io);
cards.script_api: new ImportOptions(file), ImportOptions.importAs (ImportAsType.FOOTAGE|COMP|COMP_CROPPED_LAYERS|PROJECT), .sequence, .forceAlphabetical, .rangeStart/.rangeEnd, .canImportAs(), .isFileNameNumbered(); Project.importFile(importOptions); Project.importPlaceholder(name, w, h, fps, dur)
cards.limits: Pass native absolute paths (File(path).fsName); throws if the file can't be imported. importFileWithDialog opens UI (avoid in pipelines).

cards.name: Replace footage / layer source
cards.summary: Swap what a footage item or a layer points at.
use_for: template comps whose clips are swapped per episode
cards.how: footageItem.replace(new File(path)); layer.replaceSource(otherItem, false);  replaceWithSequence / replaceWithSolid / replaceWithPlaceholder also exist.
cards.script_api: FootageItem.replace(file), replaceWithSequence(file, forceAlphabetical), replaceWithSolid(), replaceWithPlaceholder(); AVLayer.replaceSource(newSource, fixExpressions)
cards.limits: replaceSource on a null layer keeps isNull true, so the layer stays invisible. fixExpressions=true can be slow on big projects.

cards.name: Footage interpretation (FootageSource: frame rate, loop, alpha)
cards.summary: Script the Interpret Footage settings of an imported item: conform frame rate, loop count, alpha mode, fields.
use_for: conforming 25/29.97 fps news footage to the comp rate
cards.how: var src = item.mainSource; if (!src.isStill) { src.conformFrameRate = 25; src.loop = 3; } if (src.hasAlpha) src.guessAlphaMode();  // or src.alphaMode = AlphaMode.PREMULTIPLIED; src.premulColor = [0,0,0]
cards.script_api: FootageItem.mainSource / .proxySource (FootageSource): conformFrameRate (0 = native), nativeFrameRate, displayFrameRate, loop (1..9999), isStill, hasAlpha, alphaMode (AlphaMode.IGNORE|STRAIGHT|PREMULTIPLIED), premulColor, invertAlpha, fieldSeparationType, removePulldown, guessAlphaMode(), guessPulldown()
cards.limits: Setting conformFrameRate, loop or fieldSeparationType on a still throws (check isStill). conformFrameRate range 0..99. premulColor only matters with PREMULTIPLIED. Changes apply to every layer using that item.

cards.name: Project housekeeping (reduce, consolidate, fix expressions)
cards.summary: Script equivalents of File > Dependencies: reduce project, remove unused footage, consolidate, and auto-fix expressions after renames.
cards.how: app.project.reduceProject([comp]); app.project.removeUnusedFootage(); app.project.consolidateFootage(); app.project.autoFixExpressions(oldText, newText);
cards.script_api: Project.reduceProject(array_of_items), Project.removeUnusedFootage(), Project.consolidateFootage(), Project.autoFixExpressions(oldText, newText)
cards.limits: Destructive to the open project; run on a saved copy.

cards.name: Project settings (depth, color, expression engine, GPU)
cards.summary: Read/write Project Settings: bit depth, working space, linear blending, expression engine, GPU renderer, time display.
use_for: forcing 16/32 bpc for glows and gradients
cards.how: app.project.bitsPerChannel = 16; app.project.expressionEngine = 'javascript-1.0'; app.project.workingSpace = <name from app.project.listColorProfiles()>; app.project.linearBlending = true;
cards.script_api: Project.bitsPerChannel (8|16|32), Project.expressionEngine ('extendscript'|'javascript-1.0'), Project.workingSpace, Project.workingGamma, Project.linearizeWorkingSpace, Project.compensateForSceneReferredProfiles, Project.listColorProfiles(), Project.linearBlending, Project.gpuAccelType, Project.timeDisplayType
cards.limits: Setting workingSpace needs an exact profile name from listColorProfiles(). Expression syntax differs between engines (JavaScript engine is the default and faster).

cards.name: Composition settings and actions
cards.summary: CompItem attributes for size, duration, frame rate, background, work area, motion blur, renderer, plus duplicate/open.
use_for: trimming the work area before render
cards.how: comp.width/height/duration/frameRate (from AVItem); comp.bgColor = [0,0,0]; comp.workAreaStart = 0; comp.workAreaDuration = 10; comp.motionBlur = true; comp.shutterAngle = 180; comp.renderer = comp.renderers[i]; comp.duplicate(); comp.openInViewer();
cards.script_api: CompItem.bgColor, .workAreaStart, .workAreaDuration, .motionBlur, .shutterAngle, .shutterPhase, .motionBlurSamplesPerFrame, .frameBlending, .renderer, .renderers, .resolutionFactor, .draft3d, .displayStartTime, .layers, .numLayers, .selectedLayers, .duplicate(), .openInViewer(), .layer(index|name)
cards.limits: Times are seconds; frameDuration = 1/frameRate. Snap every time to the frame grid in one place (floor(t*fps+0.5)/fps) so AE and Premiere agree.

cards.name: Add layers (footage, solid, null, shape, camera, light)
cards.summary: LayerCollection methods that create each layer type.
use_for: colour solids for dips and backgrounds
cards.how: comp.layers.add(item[, stillDurationSec]); comp.layers.addSolid([r,g,b], 'BG', 1920, 1080, 1[, dur]); comp.layers.addNull([dur]); comp.layers.addShape(); comp.layers.addCamera('Cam', [960,540]); comp.layers.addLight('Key', [960,540]);
cards.script_api: LayerCollection.add(), addSolid(color, name, width, height, pixelAspect[, duration]), addNull([duration]), addShape(), addCamera(name, centerPoint), addLight(name, centerPoint), byName(name)
cards.limits: New layers go to the top (index 1) and honour the 'Create Layers at Composition Start Time' preference: set startTime/inPoint explicitly. Colors are 0-1 floats, not hex.

cards.name: Text layers: point and box (paragraph) text
cards.summary: Create point text, box (paragraph) text and vertical text layers.
use_for: wrapped paragraph text inside a fixed box
cards.how: var t = comp.layers.addText('HELLO'); var b = comp.layers.addBoxText([1650, 540]); then set Source Text: var p = b.property('Source Text'), d = p.value; d.text = 'Long caption...'; p.setValue(d);
cards.script_api: LayerCollection.addText([sourceText]), addBoxText([width, height]), addVerticalText([sourceText]) (24.2), addVerticalBoxText([width, height]) (24.2)
cards.limits: The docs list only [width, height] for addBoxText; AdobeBridge's ae_build.jsx also passes the string as an undocumented 2nd argument, but the documented route is to set Source Text afterwards. addBoxText/addText live on comp.layers (LayerCollection), not on a Layer. boxTextSize throws on point text.

cards.name: Pre-compose layers
cards.summary: Move a set of layers into a new comp and replace them with a single precomp layer.
use_for: isolating a clip for effects or a track matte
cards.how: var pc = comp.layers.precompose([2, 3], 'TXT_01', true);  // indices, name, moveAllAttributes
cards.script_api: LayerCollection.precompose(layerIndices, name[, moveAllAttributes])
cards.limits: moveAllAttributes=false is only allowed for a single layer. Returns the new CompItem; layer indices in the parent comp shift afterwards.

cards.name: Layer timing, order and copies
cards.summary: Set when a layer starts/ends, its stretch, stacking order, and duplicate or copy it to another comp.
cards.how: layer.startTime = 2.0; layer.inPoint = 2.5; layer.outPoint = 6.0; layer.stretch = 50 (=2x speed); layer.moveToBeginning(); layer.moveAfter(other); var d = layer.duplicate(); layer.copyToComp(otherComp); layer.remove();
cards.script_api: Layer.startTime, .inPoint, .outPoint, .stretch, .index, .moveBefore(), .moveAfter(), .moveToBeginning(), .moveToEnd(), .duplicate(), .copyToComp(intoComp), .remove(), .enabled, .solo, .shy, .locked, .label, .name, .activeAtTime(t)
cards.limits: inPoint/outPoint are comp time. copyToComp prepends the copy at index 1 of the target comp and returns nothing (read intoComp.layer(1)); undoing a copyToComp of a layer with effects has crashed AE (docs warning).

cards.name: Parenting
cards.summary: Parent a layer to another so it inherits transforms.
use_for: rigs: a null driving several titles
cards.how:
child.parent = nullLayer;  // keeps the child visually in place (AE offsets its transforms)
child.setParentWithJump(nullLayer);  // keeps raw transform values, so the child may jump
cards.script_api: Layer.parent, Layer.setParentWithJump([newParent])
cards.limits: Parent must be in the same comp. Set parent before keyframing if keyframe values are meant to be parent-relative.

cards.name: AVLayer switches (blend mode, 3D, adjustment, motion blur, quality)
cards.summary: Timeline switches and modes on footage/solid/text/shape layers.
use_for: Screen/Add blend for light leaks and flares
cards.how: layer.blendingMode = BlendingMode.SCREEN; layer.adjustmentLayer = true; layer.threeDLayer = true; layer.motionBlur = true; layer.quality = LayerQuality.BEST; layer.frameBlendingType = FrameBlendingType.PIXEL_MOTION; layer.guideLayer = true; layer.audioEnabled = false;
cards.script_api: AVLayer.blendingMode (BlendingMode.NORMAL|ADD|SCREEN|MULTIPLY|OVERLAY|SOFT_LIGHT|...), .adjustmentLayer, .threeDLayer, .threeDPerChar (text), .motionBlur, .quality, .samplingQuality, .frameBlendingType, .collapseTransformation (check canSetCollapseTransformation), .guideLayer, .environmentLayer, .preserveTransparency, .audioEnabled, .effectsActive
cards.limits: Comp motion blur must also be on (comp.motionBlur) for layer motion blur to render. Enum constant names are exact (note the docs spelling BlendingMode.SILHOUETE_ALPHA).

cards.name: Track mattes (setTrackMatte, AE 23.0+)
cards.summary: Since AE 23.0 any layer can use any other layer as its track matte (not just the one above) by reference.
cards.how: fill.setTrackMatte(matteLayer, TrackMatteType.ALPHA); fill.setTrackMatte(fill.trackMatteLayer, TrackMatteType.LUMA_INVERTED); fill.removeTrackMatte();
cards.script_api: AVLayer.setTrackMatte(trackMatteLayer, TrackMatteType.ALPHA|ALPHA_INVERTED|LUMA|LUMA_INVERTED), AVLayer.removeTrackMatte(), AVLayer.trackMatteLayer, AVLayer.trackMatteType (legacy setter), .hasTrackMatte, .isTrackMatte
cards.limits: setTrackMatte(layer, TrackMatteType.NO_TRACK_MATTE) is a silent no-op; pass null as the layer to remove. Setting trackMatteType directly is the legacy pre-23 API. Used in AdobeBridge vfx_build.jsx (field-tested in AdobeBridge).

cards.name: Time remapping
cards.summary: Enable time remap and keyframe source time for freeze frames, speed ramps and reverses.

templating many variants from one precomp
cards.how: var ep = precompLayer.essentialProperty.property(1); ep.setValue(...); ep.essentialPropertySource gives the original property. The Properties panel itself is UI-only.
cards.script_api: layer.property('ADBE Layer Overrides') / layer.essentialProperty, Property.essentialPropertySource (22.0)
cards.limits: Properties panel layout and its quick controls have no scripting API; everything it edits is reachable through the normal property tree. The version that first showed Essential Properties in the Properties panel (about 23.6) comes from a third-party news post and is unverified.

cards.name: Guides and rulers
cards.summary: Add, move and remove comp/layer guides (e.g. title-safe and 9:16 safe-zone guides).
use_for: marking Instagram/YouTube safe areas in templates
cards.how: comp.addGuide(1, 960);  // 1 = vertical, 0 = horizontal, position px  (26.5+: comp.addGuide(new GuideOptions()) with percent position, colour, pinning)
cards.script_api: Item.addGuide(orientationType, position), Item.setGuide(position, guideIndex), Item.removeGuide(index), Item.guides; Layer.addGuide/setGuide/removeGuide; 26.5: GuideOptions, Item.getGuideAsObject(); ViewOptions.guidesVisibility/guidesLocked/guidesSnap/rulers
cards.limits: Guides do not render. GuideOptions, GuideOrientationType/GuidePositionType and getGuideAsObject need 26.5; installed AE here is 26.0 (aerender 26.0x67), where only addGuide(0|1, px) / setGuide(px, index) exist and guides[] entries carry integers. The integer values behind orientationType/positionType change in 26.5: on 26.5+ compare against the enum constants, and gate on parseFloat(app.version). See also: 'Broadcast safe areas (action and title safe)'; 'Premiere Safe Margins and After Effects safe guides (their defaults)'; 'Platform UI safe zones (1080x1920 Reels, Shorts, TikTok)'.

cards.name: Viewer and selection control
cards.summary: Open comps in the viewer, read/set selected layers and properties, and the active tool.
cards.how: comp.openInViewer(); comp.selectedLayers; layer.selected = true; comp.time = 2.0; app.activeViewer.setActive(); app.project.toolType = ToolType.Tool_Arrow;
cards.script_api: CompItem.openInViewer(), CompItem.selectedLayers, CompItem.selectedProperties, Layer.selected, CompItem.time (via AVItem.time), app.activeViewer (Viewer.setActive(), .views, .maximized), Project.toolType
cards.limits: Selection-dependent calls (applyPreset, executeCommand) need the right comp active; viewer state is unreliable in headless/aerender runs.

cards.name: 3D: model layers, parametric meshes, cameras
cards.summary: Imported 3D models are ThreeDModelLayer (24.4+); parametric meshes can be created by script from 26.3; camera/light layers via addCamera/addLight.
cards.how: Import a .glb/.obj with app.project.importFile(...) and comp.layers.add(item) (instanceof ThreeDModelLayer). 26.3+: comp.layers.addParametricMesh('Cube', ParametricMeshType.CUBE); cam = comp.layers.addCamera('Cam', [960,540]).
cards.script_api: ThreeDModelLayer (24.4), LayerCollection.addParametricMesh(name, ParametricMeshType.SPHERE|PLANE|CYLINDER|CONE|TORUS|CUBE) (26.3), ParametricMeshLayer.parametricMeshType/.parametricMeshOptions/.parametricBevelOptions, LayerCollection.addCamera(), addLight(), CameraLayer FocusAreaWidth/NearFarBlurMultiplier (26.3, Advanced 3D only)
cards.limits: addParametricMesh needs 26.3: installed AE here is 26.0 (AfterFX.exe ProductVersion 26.0, aerender 26.0x67): gate on parseFloat(app.version) before calling. parametricMeshOptions fields depend on the type (CUBE: width, height, depth, smoothingAngle). Rendering needs the Advanced 3D renderer (comp.renderer).

cards.name: UI-only features (no scripting API)
cards.summary: Several AI/analysis tools have no documented scripting entry point: Roto Brush propagation, Content-Aware Fill, 3D Camera Tracker / Warp Stabilizer analysis control, Track Mask / tracker analysis, the Graph Editor UI, the Properties panel UI, preference panes.
use_for: deciding what a pipeline must leave to a human
routing such steps to other tools (local AI models, Premiere)
cards.how: Applying the effects is scriptable (e.g. Warp Stabilizer starts analysing on apply in the UI), but starting/controlling analysis, Roto Brush strokes and Content-Aware Fill renders are not. Some commands can be triggered with app.executeCommand on a prepared selection.
cards.script_api: none documented (fallback: app.executeCommand(id), unverified per feature)
cards.limits: Absence is inferred from the scripting guide's object model, not from an Adobe statement; treat any workaround as unverified and verify output by rendering.
